correctness.rationale: The complement of any super-dominating union omits at most two vertices; one-vertex deletions always qualify and two-vertex deletions qualify exactly at B-edges. In a four-block partition, choosing a largest block L of size>1 forces other three blocks singleton; each singleton requires a union with L and hence its opposite pair to be a B-edge, giving precisely a triangle. A nonedge yields an admissible three-block partition; when B complete, two disjoint two-sets and a remainder work because each part has at least one partner (not because every union must qualify). For three blocks, admissibility is equivalent to at least two singleton-or-B-edge small blocks and a nonsuper remaining block; counting pair types yields C(n,2)+(n-3)e+m2-2*[n=5]m2-2*[n=6]m3. Complete-multipartite case reduces B to edges between distinct qualifying non-singleton parts. Independent direct graph/set-partition enumeration checks the counting at small n.

final_claim: For isolate-free graphs of order n>=5 with gamma_sp>=n-2, c_sp=4 iff the graph of eligible two-vertex deletions contains a triangle; otherwise c_sp=3. Four-block partitions are in bijection with such triangles; all three-block coalitions have a specified binomial/edge/matching enumeration, including n=5,6 corrections.
limitations: n>=5, no isolates, gamma_sp>=n-2; no claim for unrestricted graphs.

The proof text says every pairwise union in one B-complete three-block construction works; its actual admissibility argument only requires at least one partner per block, which is correctly satisfied.
